overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding executive sessions on Feb. 5 and Feb. 20 for purposes outside Purpose 2, posting an insufficiently specific Feb. 20 notice, and approving Jan. 2 open session minutes late. It ordered release of portions of two executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board convened in executive session for an improper purpose in at least two instances; the Board identified them as February 5 and February 20.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we limit our review to these two meetings.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session under Purpose 2 (nonunion personnel negotiations) on Feb. 5 and Feb. 20, but discussed Town Administrator office challenges and a candidate's qualifications.
allegations.key_passage: Neither of these topics falls within the scope of Purpose 2.

allegations.summary: The Feb. 20 meeting notice for the Purpose 2 executive session did not identify the specific nonunion personnel who was the subject of discussion.
Complaint alleged the Board repeatedly failed to approve minutes timely, without identifying specific meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We will not conduct broad audits of a public body and thus decline to review generalized allegations about the approval practices of the Board.

allegations.summary: Open session minutes of the January 2 meeting were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board acknowledges, and we agree, that minutes of the meeting held on January 2 were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised concern that the Board does not timely review and approve executive session minutes; the letter addressed it only by reminder.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Board of its obligations under the law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Publicly release, without redaction or withholding, the portion of the February 5 executive session minutes that pertains to discussions of the Town Administrator's Office.
Publicly release, without redaction or withholding, the portion of the February 20 executive session minutes that pertains to discussion of the candidate's qualifications and background.
Notify the Attorney General in writing of compliance with the minutes-release order within 30 days of the letter's date.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
